title: FILLER — unnamed positional padding; removing or renaming silently shifts every byte after it
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RECORD-LAYOUT.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> FILLER is anonymous padding. The 4-byte FILLER between
      *> CUST-ID and CUST-NAME exists so the record matches the
      *> on-disk file layout from 1988. Removing the FILLER 'to
      *> clean up' silently shifts CUST-NAME to byte 9 and breaks
      *> every reader.
       01  CUST-RECORD.
           05  CUST-ID    PIC 9(8).
           05  FILLER     PIC X(4).
           05  CUST-NAME  PIC X(30).
           05  FILLER     PIC X(8).
           05  CUST-AMT   PIC 9(7)V99 COMP-3.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           STOP RUN.
notes: FILLER is the COBOL way to reserve bytes without naming them. Often there for historical/external-system reasons that aren't visible in the program. The spec must enumerate every FILLER and its width so the rewrite preserves the layout.
